The allocation aims to:  •	Mitigate drought impacts before crisis thresholds are reached through trigger-based early financing.  •	Protect lives, livelihoods and dignity in the most climate-exposed, severity 4+ districts.  •	Deliver integrated, household-level support, centered on multipurpose cash and early warning, complemented by agriculture, WASH, nutrition, health and protection measures.  •	Enhance speed, predictability and coherence of pooled fund responses under a unified AA framework aligned with the 2026 HNRP. This integrated approach enables more predictable, coordinated, and cost effective humanitarian action ahead of severe cyclone impacts. | The Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Asia and the Pacific (RHPF-AP) – Bangladesh envelope seeks US$150 million to support life-saving humanitarian assistance under the 2025–2026 Joint Response Plan (JRP) for the Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis and address emerging needs from natural disasters.    Bangladesh hosts over one million Rohingya refugees alongside vulnerable host communities in Cox’s Bazar, one of the country’s poorest and most disaster-prone districts. Continued displacement from Myanmar, including 130,000 new arrivals in 2025 and 35,000 expected in 2026, has intensified humanitarian needs. The 2026 JRP targets 1.56 million people, with financial requirements of US$698.4 million, including US$495.3 million in Priority 1 life-saving interventions. Funding shortfalls have heightened food insecurity, malnutrition, protection risks, and exposure to climate-related hazards.    Bangladesh also faces recurrent climate shocks—cyclones, floods, landslides, and disease outbreaks—affecting millions annually. Between 2015 and 2024, disasters affected an average of 9.7 million people per year. In 2024 alone, Cyclone Remal and widespread flooding affected 18 million people, compounding vulnerabilities in refugee-hosting areas.    Managed by OCHA’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP) under the Resident Coordinator (RC), the RHPF-AP Bangladesh envelope provides flexible, timely financing to priority sectors identified through coordinated humanitarian processes. Allocations are determined through a transparent, consultative mechanism involving an Advisory Board of local and international NGOs, UN agencies, cluster coordinators, donors, and government counterparts. Contributions are unearmarked and allocated based on agreed priorities.    The Fund operates through two windows: (i) Standard Allocations aligned with JRP priorities, and (ii) Reserve Allocations for rapid response to unforeseen emergencies. In 2026, the Fund will focus on acute food insecurity, malnutrition, inadequate WASH services, shelter and NFI gaps, health needs, protection risks including GBV and child protection, and preparedness for climate hazards. Key priorities include:    General food assistance and fresh food vouchers, with LPG support for safe cooking;    Prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women;    Emergency WASH, health services, and support to field hospitals;    Emergency shelter and NFI assistance;    Protection services for individuals at heightened risk.    The RHPF-AP emphasizes localization, prioritizing national and local partners and promoting humanitarian action that is “as local as possible, as international as necessary.” Consolidated regional management ensures cost-efficiency and compliance with OCHA’s Global Guidelines for CBPFs.    Monitoring and accountability are central. A risk-based approach prioritizes high-risk projects, with field visits, third-party monitoring where required, and remote monitoring in access-constrained areas. Robust due diligence, financial oversight, reporting, audits, and UN oversight ensure transparency. The Fund upholds strong Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) standards, including feedback mechanisms and strict compliance with the UN’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA).    Through predictable, flexible, and principled pooled financing, the RHPF-AP Bangladesh envelope strengthens coordinated humanitarian leadership, addresses funding gaps, empowers local actors, and enables timely, life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable refugees and host communities.
